raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Concurrent requests for the same externally cached prefix can allocate separate GPU destinations and transfer the prefix repeatedly. This change lets eligible requests share pending GPU blocks and wait for one load.

The block pool indexes exact pending prefixes by the existing hash/group namespace and pins their blocks with transfer-owned references. Pending entries are separate from readable prefix-cache hits; failed loads cannot be discovered, and completion removes the pending entry and releases its pins. The scheduler retains connector eligibility, request waiters, and completion/failure-policy handling. Successful loads are published before releasing an aborted initiating request. Followers cancel independently; failed readers detach before local recomputation. Pending loads prevent connector-cache resets.

Initial support is explicitly opt-in for the built-in CPUOffloadingSpec with built-in LRU/ARC policies: prefix caching enabled, one FullAttentionSpec group, exact contiguous block-aligned partial-prompt prefixes, including prefixes extending a local hit. Full-prompt loads, speculation, context parallelism, encoder inputs, custom specs/policies, and other connectors retain existing behavior. Cache salts and token-hash isolation are preserved.

Addresses #44882. Duplicate checks covered issue comments, open PRs referencing the issue, and area searches. #48189 closed unmerged; #44295 changes connector convoy handling, rather than shared core allocation/lifetime. #53067 and #55724 address connector context and admission. NIXL is being pursued as a separate follow-up by NolenLiang.

Local validation on October 18, against main `f26d9f432c`:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py \
  -q --tb=short --maxfail=3 --confcutdir=tests/v1
```

**650 passed**, including 14 deferred-free tests. The prior four-file suite had 636 passes, independently rerun by the human submitter on October 15 at `367746fff7`. Two lifecycle tests now acknowledge their final scheduled computation before asserting cleanup. Enabling deferred frees locally reproduced nine cleanup failures before this correction; all 16 selected lifecycle cases pass afterward. No production behavior was changed by this test correction (proposed by LysanderPhong). Coverage includes shared allocation/loading, transfer pins after all request references are released, pending/cache separation, group isolation, duplicate registration, initiating-request/follower cancellation, late followers, local-prefix extension, both failure policies, block/request receive failures (including aborted owners), queue/statistics cleanup, and reference/job cleanup. CPU-offload scheduler integration emits one logical load job in sync/async scheduling modes; worker completion is simulated. The earlier four request-level failure regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward.

`.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <eight changed files>` passed all applicable hooks, including mypy (Python 3.11 target), ruff, test tethering, and SPDX. `git diff origin/main --check` passed.

External GPU/model evidence: [LysanderPhong's October 18 rerun](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418#issuecomment-6245502608) validates production source `367746fff7` with the official `f26d9f432c` native wheel on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (WSL, Torch 2.13.0+cu130):

- Ten native CPU↔GPU cases passed: sync/async sharing, opt-out, initiating-request cancellation with a late follower, follower/all-reader cancellation, and receive-completion failure under both policies with live/aborted owners. Checks cover exact FP16 bytes, destinations held out of the free queue while CUDA end events remain incomplete, private tails, and cleanup. Failures were injected after successful copies, not genuine transport/CUDA-copy faults.
- Qwen3-0.6B FP16: one 257-token prompt, eight concurrent requests, 16 greedy tokens. Sharing-on observed seven followers; opt-out observed none. All output token IDs matched between modes and uncached seed outputs. Both modes completed one 28 MiB load; this establishes no transfer-volume/performance improvement or broad accuracy result.

GPU/model execution was contributor-reported and agent-executed, not independently rerun here or manually human-attested. The large evidence fixtures are not included in this diff. Hi @zayedu. I'm coming at the same problem from the RL side. In GRPO-style rollout we sample n responses per prompt, so a group of requests shares one long prefix and hits the decode instance at roughly the same time. Under PD with NIXL that prefix gets pulled n times: when the siblings are scheduled, the first load hasn't published to the prefix cache yet, so none of them hit.

Your PR looks like it already covers the core of that — the shared block and refcount, the supports_shared_prefix_loads() contract, and the owner/follower abort and failure paths. What I don't think is covered yet is NIXL, which brings its own questions: what makes two requests safe to share (model/KV namespace, TP layout, the per-request transfer lease on the P side), keeping the pull alive when the owner aborts while followers are still waiting, and making sure each P-side request still gets released.

1. Is extending this to NIXL already on your roadmap? If so I'd rather help

2. If not, would you be open to me picking that piece up on top of your
   contract? I'd work against your branch and follow whatever shape you've
   settled on.

The implementation will cover compatibility checks, keeping the owner's transfer and lease alive through cancellation while readers remain, and releasing every producer-side request.

`failed_recving` also needs to mark the shared load as failed. The connector contract guarantees that failed receives are included in `finished_recving`, but `_complete_shared_prefix_load()` only observes failures reported through `invalid_block_ids`.
